Every other graded rule's text is unchanged and graded to the standard's bar.

"Assert with patterns" changed; graded against the current text. The sentence that now decides the `==` verdicts: "The value under test goes on the left of `==` and the expected value on the right, whether it is the call itself or a result bound a line earlier: a failure prints left and right in that order, so `assert {:ok, "ch_1"} == result` reads as if the literal were on trial." The three sentences are counted separately. (a) The `==` sentence: 0 of 4 violate (standard: 2 of 5, haiku-1's assert {:ok, "ch_1"} == result and sonnet-2's assert {:ok, "ch_123"} == Charger.charge(...)). Every `==` assertion, with the side holding the value under test: haiku-1 line 27: assert result == {:ok, "ch_1"}; line 41: assert result == {:error, :declined}; line 50: assert result == {:error, :unavailable} (result, bound a line earlier from with_log, on the left). haiku-2 line 40: assert result == {:ok, "ch_1"}; line 55: assert result == {:error, :declined}; line 69: assert result == {:error, :unavailable} (bound result on the left). sonnet-1 lines 43-44: assert Charger.charge(1_250, "tok_1", gateway: ApprovingGateway, request_id: "req_1") == / {:ok, "ch_1"}; lines 62-63: assert Charger.charge(1_250, "tok_1", gateway: DecliningGateway, request_id: "req_2") == / {:error, :declined}; lines 83-84: assert Charger.charge(900, "tok_1", gateway: UnavailableGateway, request_id: "req_3") == / {:error, :unavailable} (the call on the left); line 55: assert log == "" (captured log on the left). sonnet-2 lines 41-42: assert Charger.charge(1_500, "tok_1", gateway: ApprovingGateway, request_id: "req_1") == / {:ok, "ch_1"}; lines 62-63: assert Charger.charge(1_500, "tok_1", gateway: DecliningGateway, request_id: "req_2") == / {:error, :declined}; lines 84-85: assert Charger.charge(900, "tok_1", gateway: UnavailableGateway, request_id: "req_3") == / {:error, :unavailable} (the call on the left); line 55: assert log == "" (captured log on the left). No `!=` and no expected value on the left anywhere. haiku-1 and haiku-2 bind result through a with_log destructure and compare it whole with ==; the standard needed a judgment for that shape (its opus-1, graded clean against the "binds the value and an == on it afterwards" sentence); the current text names "a result bound a line earlier" as a left-hand side, so it now decides these as clean. (b) The bare-match sentence ("In a test body, every match that can fail takes `assert` in front ... A destructure that cannot fail, such as `{result, log} = with_log(...)`, needs none.", unchanged): 0 of 4 violate (standard: 0 of 5). The only bare matches are with_log destructures: haiku-1 lines 25, 31, 39, 48 ({result, _log} = with_log(@log_format, fn -> charge("tok_accepted") end)); haiku-2 lines 38, 44, 53, 59, 67, 73 ({result, _log} = charge("tok_ok", 250)), where charge/2 (lines 20-34) returns with_log's tuple unchanged, so the destructure cannot fail and the exemption covers it (judgment: the call is a helper, not with_log by name). sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 bind only plain variables (log = capture_log(...)). Every match that can fail has assert (sonnet-1 lines 51, 70, 91; sonnet-2 lines 51, 70, 92). (c) The wrap-every-call sentence of the capture rule ("Wrap every call that logs, the ones whose return value is under test included, so the suite prints nothing.", unchanged): 0 of 4 break it (standard: 0 of 5). haiku-1 calls charge/3 only through its helper charge/2 (line 56) and calls that only inside with_log (lines 25, 31, 39, 48); haiku-2 only inside with_log in charge/2 (lines 21-33); sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 wrap the return-value tests in option-less capture_log/1 (sonnet-1 lines 42, 61, 82; sonnet-2 lines 40, 61, 83) and the log tests in capture_log with options. Confirmed in practice: no run prints a log line (see the test-run note).

"Capture logs with `capture_log/2`, not a handler" (unchanged) is clean in 4 of 4: no :logger.add_handler, StringIO device, backend, Logger.configure or Logger.put_module_level (the primary-level sentence stays unprovoked). haiku-1: @log_format [format: "$level $metadata$message\n", metadata: :all, colors: [enabled: false]] (line 21); with_log in every test; metadata asserted with line-anchored regexes (lines 43-44); success absence by refute log =~ ~r/^(warning|error) /m (line 35) after an info-line assertion (line 34), a regex that leaves out critical, alert and emergency, as in the standard's haiku-1. haiku-2: options [format: @log_format, metadata: [:request_id, :charge_id, :amount_cents], colors: [enabled: false]] inline in with_log inside its charge/2 helper (lines 21-26); metadata asserted as one exact anchored line (line 61, error line 75); success absence by refute log =~ ~r/^(emergency|alert|critical|error|warning) /m (line 47) after line 46. sonnet-1: @log_options with format, metadata [:request_id, :amount_cents, :charge_id] and colors (lines 10-14); metadata as level-prefixed and plain substrings (lines 74-76); success absence by capture_log([level: :warning] ++ @log_options, ...) and assert log == "" (lines 50, 55). sonnet-2: @log_options with format, metadata [:request_id, :amount_cents] and colors (lines 31-35); metadata as separate substrings (lines 74-77); success absence by capture_log([level: :warning], ...), without format options, and assert log == "" (lines 50, 55), the standard's sonnet-2 shape.

As in the standard, each file was run against five mutants of the input (success logs at warning, declined logs at info, declined drops amount_cents, Logger.metadata(request_id: ...) removed, unavailable logs at warning instead of error): every file fails at least one test on every mutant (haiku-1 1 of 4 each; haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2 1 of 6 each, 2 of 6 on the request_id mutant), so no log assertion is vacuous; sonnet-2's loose assert log =~ "error" (line 96) still fails when the unavailable path logs at warning.

"Group tests by function and name them by behaviour", "Run tests concurrently unless they share global state" and "Replace dependencies at boundaries, through behaviours" are unchanged and clean in 4 of 4. haiku-1 uses one describe "charge/3" with condition-bearing names (line 38: test "returns :declined and logs a warning with the request id and amount" do, which names the decline reason and the log, not only that the call did not fail); the other three use describe "charge/3" plus a condition. All four use async: true with no Logger.configure, Process.register or application env. haiku-1 and haiku-2 use one Payments.Gateway module answering by token (haiku-2's with a catch-all approving clause, line 15); sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 use one module per outcome nested in the test module.

Outside the case's list: haiku-2 breaks "Build a multi-line argument under a name before the call" in charge/2, where with_log's options keyword list spans lines 22-26 inside the call and charge/3's options span lines 28-31, the shape the standard reported for its sonnet-1; and "Before you finish" step 1: the session never ran mix format, it wrote the file with elixir -e 'f = "charger_test.exs"; File.write!(f, [IO.iodata_to_binary(Code.format_file!(f)), "\n"])', which left an extra blank line at line 79 after the final end, so mix format --check-formatted fails (confirming format_ok false in result.json; the only diff is that line). Not reported, as in the standard: sonnet-2's nested gateway modules have no @moduledoc false in an .exs script that builds no docs.

Tests were run from copies in the scratch folder with elixir -r log-tests-input.ex charger_test.exs on Elixir 1.20.4, 20 times each with random seeds: every file passed every time (haiku-1 4 tests, the others 6) with no compiler warning and no line printed beyond ExUnit's own, which confirms the wrap-every-call sentence in practice. haiku-1, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 pass mix format --check-formatted; haiku-2 fails on the trailing blank line 79.
